correctness.rationale: The indexed unit-step coefficient sum is a Zak multiplication operator. On each unit cell the tent has just two adjacent terms, with a nonnegative cross coefficient, so frequency 0 simultaneously maximizes all contributions and frequency 1/2 minimizes them. Continuity identifies extrema with essential extrema. This gives the stated m and circular least-squares bounds even with repeated offsets. Independently, A/4 is the squared distance of the projected phase vector to the lattice P Z^m in the orthogonal complement of the diagonal, with P orthogonal projection; minimizing over the common real center and all integer lifts gives this identity. The images of e_2,...,e_m form a lattice basis with Gram determinant 1/m. A nonconstant integer vector has at least m-1 unequal unordered pairs, so the shortest nonzero projected lattice vector has length sqrt((m-1)/m), attained by e_1. The ball of radius sqrt(a)/2 for the stated 0<a<1/4 injects into the quotient. Haar probability is its Euclidean volume divided by lattice covolume 1/sqrt(m), exactly the stated expression. Substitution gives the Pareto coefficient; integrating the tail gives the strict moment cutoff and logarithmic divergence at the threshold. For m=2, the shorter-distance law gives A=2 delta^2 and kappa=delta^(-2), including the stated K=4 endpoint. Read VERIFICATION.md and CHECK.py as evidence; the frozen rational/grid tests were not run and are not the proof.
